notes: A compound crest surviving only stitched on a shirt (ring + rule + shield + ram's head, with a fold shadow across the right third), two hand-drawn glyph sheets a decade apart on graph paper (monoline digits vs modulated letters, O drawn twice, Q and apostrophe missing), last season's back-of-shirt PDF, a 24-player squad with a repeated surname / duplicate number / un-fittable name / apostrophe, and two badly-lit blank shirts that disagree on colour.

assets.prompt: Close handheld phone photograph of a football club crest EMBROIDERED on the breast of a claret home shirt laid flat on a kitchen table under a single ceiling light. It is a COMPOUND lockup in satin-stitch and chain-stitch THREAD (not ink): an outer RING of claret small-caps lettering reading 'RIDGEWAY ROVERS FC' with '1974' at the base, a FINE HAIRLINE RULE stitched just inside the ring, a SHIELD in the centre, and inside the shield a RAM'S HEAD in old-gold and navy thread. Raised stitch texture, slightly scalloped/ragged thread edges. Across the RIGHT THIRD of the crest the shirt is slightly folded so it sits in a FOLD SHADOW where the navy thread of the ram's head and the claret cloth run very close in value. A soft fabric wrinkle, everyday indoor snapshot, slight handheld softness.
assets.defect_engineered: compound stitched lockup — one selection naming the crest returns the ring + shield outline but silently drops the hairline rule and the ram's head; naming the garment pulls to the cloth; a one-call knockout on the enclosed ring returns a solid disc; the right third sits in a fold shadow where navy thread and claret cloth run close in value

assets.prompt: Overhead phone photograph of a hand-drawn reference sheet on a kitchen table: a full uppercase ALPHABET drawn in black marker on PALE-BLUE GRIDDED GRAPH PAPER. The letters are drawn with a MODULATED CHISEL-TIP stroke that visibly THICKENS at every join and corner (broad-nib feel), slightly irregular by hand, in a sturdy slab character. Laid out in rows. CRUCIAL QUIRKS: the letter O is drawn TWICE (appears in two cells) and the letter Q is MISSING entirely from the sheet; there is NO apostrophe or punctuation anywhere. The pale-blue printed graph grid is clearly visible behind and between the letters (dark enough to read as its own lines). Slight paper cockle, a table edge and a marker pen at the margin, warm kitchen light.
assets.defect_engineered: modulated chisel stroke (thickens at joins) drawn a decade after the digits with a different pen; the pale-blue graph rule is dark enough to survive a trace as its own geometry; O drawn twice, Q omitted, no apostrophe anywhere

LAYOUT DESCRIPTION (for the renderer/author of this press PDF)

Product: back-of-shirt sign-off sheet, the supplier's own studio format. A4 portrait, ONE player per page. Genuine press PDF. No bleed present and none can be added from this file.

Appearance: Navy (#1E2A44) header band reading 'RIDGEWAY ROVERS FC — BACK OF SHIRT' with a small crest; Shirt White (#F4F2ED) ground.
  Centre: a large preview showing the arched NAME set above the NUMBER exactly as it prints on the shirt back.
  Lower block: variable fields, plus a sign-off line 'Approved by parent/guardian ____'.

IMPORTANT STRUCTURE: the variable fields are set as a THREADED TEXT FLOW (one story), not separate labelled frames.

FIELD CONTENT in the story, in order:
  NAME
  NUMBER
  INITIAL
  SIZE

Example values on last season's sheet (last year's captain):
  NAME MORLEY | NUMBER 4 | INITIAL D | SIZE L
assets.defect_engineered: variable fields set as one threaded story; the converted document's text readout drops one run while keeping its line break, so offsets past it fall short, the validator reports valid and the build reports success while two of five fields never land; no bleed and none can be introduced

assets.content:
RIDGEWAY ROVERS FC — KIT SUPPLIER NOTE
(what the supplier told us they can actually do)

WHAT WE CAN RUN
  Heat-press vinyl and flock. ONE spot colour per element on numbering and lettering: no gradients, no inline, no keyline, no second colour on numbers.
  Crest: up to 3 spot colours for the breast (claret / navy / old gold). A single-ink crest is required for the training tops, and a version that holds on the navy away shirt.

CUT AND HEAT-PRESS CONSTRAINTS
  Every glyph must be a SINGLE closed solid shape, generously weighted. Minimum limb/stroke width 4 mm at back-of-shirt size. No thin joins. No open counters (an enclosed counter is cut as an island only if it is 6 mm or wider).
  Back-of-shirt NUMBER height 250 mm; NAME arched above, cap height 65 mm.
  Breast crest height 80 mm; sleeve crest 55 mm.

PLACEMENT HEIGHTS
  Back number centred, top of digits 180 mm below the collar seam.
  Name arched above the number, baseline 30 mm above the digits.
  Breast crest on the left breast, 150 mm below the shoulder seam.

COLOURS (confirm against artwork)
  Claret 6B1F2E | Navy 1E2A44 | Old Gold C09A3E | Shirt White F4F2ED.

BACK-OF-SHIRT SHEET
  One player per page in OUR format (see last year's PDF): NAME, NUMBER, INITIAL, SIZE, small crest.
  Repeated surnames carry a forename INITIAL in front (our rule).
  No bleed on our sheet.

DEADLINE
  Artwork required by the end of the month for the coming season.
assets.defect_engineered: none (clean reference: single-spot-colour cuttable rule, 4 mm minimum limb, glyph/crest heights, placement heights, the repeated-surname initial rule)
